statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-42257 (GHSA-hm49-wcqc-g2xg): before net-imap 0.4.24, 0.5.14 and 0.6.4, several Net::IMAP commands sent certain String arguments to the server as raw data without validation (criteria for #search, #sort and #thread and their UID forms, attr for #fetch and #store and their UID forms, and the #setquota limit), so a CRLF sequence in user-controlled input could inject further IMAP commands: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/security/advisories/GHSA-hm49-wcqc-g2xg. On the 0.5 release line it is fixed in net-imap 0.5.14 by https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/pull/662, merge commit https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/commit/6bf02aef7e0b5931010c36e377f79a71636b306b, which is in v0.5.14 and not in v0.5.13: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/releases/tag/v0.5.14. As of 2026-11-27 the DHI ruby-3.4 package for Alpine 3.23 is published as 3.4.8-r0, 3.4.8-r1, 3.4.9-r1, 3.4.9-r2, 3.4.10-r2, 3.4.10-r3, 3.4.11-r3, 3.4.12-r3, 3.4.13-r3 and 3.4.13-r4, for x86_64 and aarch64. It ships net-imap in its ruby3.4-net-imap gem package, which carries the gem's version rather than Ruby's, so the range below is written in ruby-3.4 versions and each ruby-3.4 build is placed by the net-imap its build produced. We downloaded every package built from the ruby-3.4 source in that repository for both architectures, 432 package files, each checked against its repository index checksum, and listed every file in them. net-imap is installed only by ruby3.4-net-imap; the only other net-imap file is a cached gem archive, usr/lib/ruby/gems/3.4.0/cache/net-imap-0.5.14.gem, in ruby-3.4-libs 3.4.9-r2, which holds net-imap 0.5.14 and is not loaded: Ruby loads net-imap from the installed gem directory. Net::IMAP::VERSION in lib/net/imap.rb of each published ruby3.4-net-imap package: 0.5.8 in 0.5.8-r0 and 0.5.8-r1, 0.5.14 in 0.5.8-r2 (despite its label), and 0.5.15 in 0.5.15-r2, 0.5.15-r3 and 0.5.15-r4. The RawData validation the fix adds to lib/net/imap/command_data.rb (its error message 'RawData cannot end with literal continuation' is absent at v0.5.13 and present at v0.5.14) is in the 0.5.14 and 0.5.15 packages and absent from both 0.5.8 packages, on both architectures. The repository index gives each gem package the same build time and source commit as the ruby-3.4 build that produced it: 0.5.8-r0 with 3.4.8-r0, 0.5.8-r1 with 3.4.9-r1, 0.5.8-r2 with 3.4.9-r2, 0.5.15-r2 with 3.4.10-r2, 0.5.15-r3 with 3.4.13-r3 and 0.5.15-r4 with 3.4.13-r4. The gem packages of the other four builds were replaced in the repository by later builds of the same package version. 3.4.8-r1 is Ruby 3.4.8, which bundles net-imap 0.5.8 (gems/bundled_gems at the v3_4_8 tag), and its ruby-3.4-libs carries no replacement net-imap archive, so it ships 0.5.8. 3.4.10-r3, 3.4.11-r3 and 3.4.12-r3 are Ruby releases that bundle net-imap 0.5.15 (gems/bundled_gems at the v3_4_10, v3_4_11 and v3_4_12 tags), and 0.5.15-r3 is the only gem package version published with their -r3 release number. Ruby 3.4.9 also bundles net-imap 0.5.8; 3.4.9-r2 is the build that replaced it with 0.5.14. So 3.4.8-r0, 3.4.8-r1 and 3.4.9-r1 ship a net-imap without the fix, and the range ends at 3.4.9-r2, the first build that ships net-imap 0.5.14.

CVE-2026-42257 (GHSA-hm49-wcqc-g2xg): in the Ruby net-imap gem, several Net::IMAP commands pass caller-supplied strings to the server as raw protocol data without validating them, so an application that forwards untrusted input can be made to send additional IMAP commands (command injection): https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/security/advisories/GHSA-hm49-wcqc-g2xg. Upstream fixed it in net-imap 0.4.24 on the 0.4 line, 0.5.14 on the 0.5 line and 0.6.4 on the 0.6 line; the 0.6.4 release notes list GHSA-hm49-wcqc-g2xg: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/releases/tag/v0.6.4. The DHI ruby-4.0 package for Alpine 3.23 is published as 4.0.1-r0, 4.0.1-r1, 4.0.2-r1, 4.0.2-r2, 4.0.3-r2, 4.0.4-r2, 4.0.4-r3, 4.0.5-r3, 4.0.6-r3, 4.0.6-r4, 4.0.7-r4, 4.0.9-r4, 4.0.10-r4 and 4.0.10-r5, for x86_64 and aarch64. It ships net-imap in its ruby4.0-net-imap gem package, which carries the gem's version rather than Ruby's, so the range below is written in the ruby-4.0 package's own versions, and each ruby-4.0 build is placed by the net-imap its ruby4.0-net-imap package installs. The gem package keeps the gem's own version but takes its -rN release number from the Ruby build that produced it, and the repository keeps one copy of each package version, so the gem package versions published under a given -rN are exactly the net-imap releases the Ruby builds with that -rN shipped. We read Net::IMAP::VERSION in lib/net/imap.rb of every published ruby4.0-net-imap package for both architectures, each verified against the repository index checksum, and listed the contents of every published ruby-4.0-libs package: the published ruby4.0-net-imap packages are 0.6.2-r0, 0.6.2-r1, 0.6.2-r2, 0.6.2-r3, 0.6.4.1-r3, 0.6.4.1-r4 and 0.6.4.1-r5. 0.6.2-r0, -r1 and -r2 install net-imap 0.6.2, the only gem version under -r0, -r1 and -r2, so 4.0.1-r0 through 4.0.4-r2 ship 0.6.2. Under -r3 two gem versions exist: 0.6.2-r3, which despite its label installs net-imap 0.6.4, and 0.6.4.1-r3, which installs net-imap 0.6.4.1. The 4.0.4-r3 and 4.0.5-r3 builds are the ones that replaced their bundled net-imap with 0.6.4: ruby-4.0-libs 4.0.4-r3 and 4.0.5-r3 both carry the net-imap-0.6.4 gem archive that install left behind, while no other ruby-4.0-libs build carries a net-imap archive; 4.0.6-r3 ships 0.6.4.1. 0.6.4.1-r4 and 0.6.4.1-r5 install net-imap 0.6.4.1, so 4.0.6-r4, 4.0.7-r4, 4.0.9-r4, 4.0.10-r4 and 4.0.10-r5 ship 0.6.4.1. Both architectures agree for every build. Every ruby-4.0 build before 4.0.4-r3 ships a net-imap without this fix, and 4.0.4-r3 is the first that ships net-imap 0.6.4, so the range is introduced at the first published build and fixed at 4.0.4-r3.
